messages:
alex: Quick newbie question /
I start on 2026-04-29 and notice our office holiday (company-wide day off) is 2026-05-01. Am I eligible for holiday pay even though I'm not through my first full pay period? Also will benefits (health/dental) be active for any services on 2026-05-01? cc @lisa :wave:
lisa: Welcome Alex! Short answers: 1) Holiday pay eligibility depends on your employment status on the holiday (you must be an active employee on the holiday and not on unpaid leave). Start date 2026-04-29 means you are active on 2026-05-01, so you should get holiday pay. 2) Benefits effective date depends on your enrollment election. Did you enroll during your new-hire window?
alex: I completed enrollment during onboarding (submitted on 2026-04-30). The benefits portal shows an effective date of 2026-06-01. Which means not covered on 5/1. Is there any exception for company holidays?
benefits-bot: Enrollment received. Carrier effective date: 2026-06-01. Carrier policies control coverage start; company holidays do not change carrier effective dates. For urgent care between start and effective date, submit receipts to Expensify with category `healthcare-reimbursements` for retro review. See: https://redwood.intranet/benefits/enroll :link:
lisa: Thanks bot. Alex 97 sorry about the mismatch. Holiday pay is separate from carrier coverage; HR will file holiday payroll as a paid day off. For medical coverage, we can request a carrier exception (sometimes approved for urgent services) but not guaranteed. If you need to file for a holiday-day domestic travel reimbursement or commute credit, commuter benefits have a separate enrollment cutoff (first of month after enrollment).
tom-payroll: Payroll note: Holiday pay will be processed automatically for active new hires. It will appear on the payroll run covering 2026-05-15 as a paid holiday line item, not charged to PTO. No action needed. For any retro benefits reimbursement that payroll issues (if carrier approves or we reimburse directly), it will be processed as a separate vendor payment and not lumped into regular wages, unless flagged taxable.
jess: Small gotcha: if you were marked as "no-show" on the holiday or on an unpaid leave day, holiday pay could be voided. Since you're onboarding that week, keep your manager looped so you have approved status for that day.
alex: Good to know  thanks. If I had a dentist appointment on 5/1 (routine) and carrier denies retro, would I still be able to submit for reimbursement through the company FSA or dependent-care? Which category do I pick in Expensify?
lisa: Use `healthcare-reimbursements` for medical/dental. If you elected FSA and the plan year is active, FSA claims should be submitted to the FSA vendor directly (we provide the vendor link) not Expensify. Expensify is for ad-hoc reimbursements via People Ops when carrier retro is needed or for non-FSA ad-hoc processing. If your FSA wasn't active yet, file through People Ops as a retro review.
alex: Ok copying the steps: 1) holiday pay auto-applied, 2) upload dentist receipt to Expensify under `healthcare-reimbursements` and open ticket if retro needed, 3) coordinate with manager to confirm holiday status. Thanks everyone! :smile:
lisa: Exactly. If you want, drop your Expensify report ID here after upload and we'll watch for it. Also FYI copy-paste memo to use:
``
Provider: Midtown Dental
Date of service: 2026-05-01
Service: Routine cleaning
Amount: $92.00
Category: healthcare-reimbursements
Notes: New-hire retro request; benefits effective 2026-06-01. Please escalate to benefits admin for carrier review.
``
alex: Will do / uploading now. Appreciate the clarity :raised_hands:
